title: Lot Genealogy, Affected Scope and Evidence-Bounded Investigation

content.overview: Affected scope should follow genealogy and shared process exposure, not fear or convenience. Technician II traces source harvest identity through racks, lots, movements, rooms and storage, then defines what evidence supports inclusion or exclusion from the investigation.

vocabulary.definition: The traceable relationship between source material and downstream lots, containers, movements or process states.
The evidence-supported set of material, locations or time periods potentially involved in the deviation.
A process, room, equipment, movement or time condition plausibly common to multiple material units.

sections.title: Trace from source to current identity
sections.body: Preserve source harvest/batch identity when material is divided, moved or relabeled into downstream process units. New identifiers extend genealogy rather than erase it.

sections.title: Scope narrowly when evidence supports narrow scope
sections.body: If only one traceable rack shared the relevant condition, do not automatically label the entire facility affected. Conversely, do not exclude connected material simply to improve apparent results.

sections.title: Document why material enters or leaves the investigation
sections.body: Scope decisions should cite identity, shared exposure, position, timeline and product evidence rather than undocumented assumptions.

workedExamples: A room excursion overlaps only two traceable lots during a defined window; other lots were in a different room and time period, so scope starts with the shared exposure evidence.
A rack was moved through the same affected drying zone before the deviation was noticed; its genealogy and timing keep it in the investigation until evidence supports exclusion.
commonMistakes: Scoping the whole facility by default.
Excluding failed or suspect material from the dataset.
Losing source genealogy when assigning a downstream lot number.
Changing identifiers to make records agree.
content.practicalApplication: Draw a lot-genealogy diagram linking harvest source, racks, rooms, movements, sampling and current status, then annotate inclusion/exclusion evidence for affected scope.
content.summary: Defensible scope follows traceable genealogy and shared process evidence, neither broader nor narrower than the records support.

primaryVisuals.title: Lot genealogy and evidence-bounded affected scope
primaryVisuals.alt: Lot genealogy flow tracing source harvest identity through racks, rooms, movements and downstream lot identifiers, then using shared exposure, position, timing and product evidence to include or exclude material from affected scope without making the investigation automatically facility-wide or artificially narrow.
primaryVisuals.caption: Affected scope follows traceable genealogy and shared exposure. Include and exclude material because the evidence supports it, not because a broader or narrower scope is more convenient.
